page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 7.0 GB of RAM. It runs on the x86_64 architecture using a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.3 GHz and features a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2081.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 34.12 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics are weaker. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated in the bottom 10%, and the uncached memory read bandwidth is limited to 15.64 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 3.03 million operations per second, which is also on the lower end of the performance spectrum.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-2 serves as a low-cost entry point to Google Cloud's dedicated Intel Xeon c4 family. It provides access to advanced hardware instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) without requiring a large resource footprint. Due to its strong single-threaded performance but constrained memory bandwidth, this instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments.
